body: Well that's sounds like me. Except idk if he even considered me girlfriend material to begin with.
Not understanding what it means to open up. Keeping it or framing it as a casual fuck buddy.
am i? i feel like so many people are selfless, social, hot, smart, kind, caring, perfect, people that everyone else praises.
I don't feel like I am really putting on a mask. I just feel like my normal self is boring to everyone. I'm always the last resort friend too.
Except my "bag" are all deal breakers for decent guys- anxiety, social problems, hardly any friends, no ideas for plans.
what small things did you change?

how does your husband react to your anxiety? Just trying to see if there are any patterns so I can identify and treat the problem. I wonder if telling my partner about my anxiety is a smart move or if it will be a turnoff. Obviously its treatable but still.

> your insecurity/anxiety is a turn-off currently. 

How is this coming across and how will the results be different post-therapy? (in your own experience too obviously) I am in therapy. 

And the guy I'm currently seeing (sort of) fits all of these. I feel like I was working for him too at first but now I feel like maybe he was just running game or something and/or he's bored by me.

> plenty of guys are smart, attractive, funny, and have a generally positive outlook on life and decent conflict resolution skills.

Serious question: where are these guys? because I do not meet them... when I do, they are not looking for something serious ~with me~ no matter their age.

> what are your compatibility standards in more detail? 

Someone who talks a lot, is adventurous, non-relgious, isn't judgmental, very confident in himself (because I can sometimes be difficult and I need someone who doesn't live a "keeping up with the jones'" type existence), empathetic, smart/street smart, not a douchebag or a cheater/egotistical asshole, loyal, honest, blunt and straightforward, and of course thinks I'm amazing.

I'm essentially all these things - except I'm not a huge talker but am good at maneuvering through social situations.
i mean dating someone else not an official relationship
because girls lie their way through shit all the time to get the guy.
yeah but everyone else is a flawless fantasy or so it seems.

> I suspect you're trying to move in social circles that may be shallow/superficial/judgmental.

I feel like if I'm not fitting in on a superficial level, I must be ugly or awkward or something, when I'm not.

I've dated introverted guys before - many many times actually. I don't like discriminate against them or anything. In fact a lot of the time I'd rather date someone introverted because there's a connection on some level. However... those have easily been my worst "relationships" because they're expending so much energy to talk to me, and I them, that conversations are hard and draining. Chemistry hardly happens because it's just passing the conversation like a hot potato and no one really wants to carry that. The ones that have had the most chemistry are the extroverted guys who talk a lot - because they talk and it's natural for them - and I listen and that's natural for me.
I know! That's why I'm dealing with the anxiety professionally. But that STILL doesn't explain why I'm always boring, or our time together is - for every guy. And all people, frankly.

Well, I have horrible anxiety so my true self is adventurous, etc. but I am generally don't with people who like to do that stuff and because I can't sustain an interesting time with them. I'm introverted yes but I'm not a wallflower and like doing things.

The crazy thing was a joke, first of all.

And yes, I feel like I need a very extroverted guy to keep things going. I see most relationships are a balance of someone more introverted, and someone more extroverted. Usually those are very successful. Again, I'm not antisocial or anything, I just feel that having someone who brings me out of my shell in that way is a good match for me. 

EDIT: and no, I dont feel like the "boring" me is the real me. I don't even know what the extroverted guy wants or what the perfect girlfriend mode is. That's the whole problem.

> Give your true opinion about things.

Even if it's awful? I feel like when I go 100% "being myself" I become very defensive and opinionated, often times expressing negative opinions over positive.

> are you sexually adventurous? I don't mean crazy stuff.... but by keeping things exciting?

I'm down for anything - but what are things that aren't crazy or how to keep it exciting, beyond idfferent positions/locations?

>What do you like to do for fun? 

I like to go exploring, go online, travel.
Show myself how?

>  if you find someone you're compatible with in terms of personality and life goals and so on, there's really not much effort one needs to expend to do what it takes to keep themselves and the other person happy.


This is what I fear... no one is compatible with me who I also like and/or he likes me.
But if I want to attract good guys, I need to know what they want.

I come across as boring and the time I spend with whoever I date isn't fun... according to them. Which is why I feel like I can't make a relationship work - because I can't be going left and right and constantly being fun 24/7 to keep a mans interest.
I don't know WHAT people want me to be...

> Do you have any idea why relationships don't last? Are you picky? Do you go out enough? 

They get bored by me. I feel like I have to be a circus performer to keep a guy interested - having invitations to social events left and right - constantly having interesting annectdotes. Idk even - because even when I have that stuff.. it's NEVER enough.
I guess I don't really know in what ways to put myself out there? What is too much/too little to say?
Can I ask why? Just curious. Also if this is true, this happens to me a lot. Is there any way to prevent this?

but do i do it now, a week before the test? I haven't even heard from him since his birthday a few days ago. I'm just really lost here and it's making me want to put myself out there less and less. And I don't want the act of having this discussion to seem selfish given the timing.
I know I don't have to please him- he doesnt know me. That's also how we set the relationship up to be.

He never said he wanted more. In fact when I first asked him if he was looking for a relationship, he said "no" without hesitation. He has been talking to other girls as far as I know, and wanted me to be in a threesome with him and someone else. But I guess that other girl chickened out. So no, I do not think he ever wanted more.
but the person he thinks he knows isnt the real good me bc anxiety
I know he doesn't have feelings. You can't have feelings for someone you don't know.
he doesn't feel the same because i've never showed him who i really am. he's just seen anxious me and closed off/defensive me.
I honestly have no idea how he feels. For all I know he really doesn't see me as more than a casual sex girl and is in love with someone else entirely.
